# Virtualization entity refinements

Entity refinements specialize upstream OpenTelemetry entities with additional
identity and description attributes specific to the
Virtualization domain.

| Refinement ID | Refined Entity Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `refinement.virtualization.partition.host` | `host` | Refinement of the generic host entity for a firmware-enforced partition. A virtualization partition is a hardware-isolated execution environment — the mainframe equivalent of a virtual machine, but enforced at the firmware level. The partition behaves as an independent host from the perspective of workloads running inside it. |
| `refinement.virtualization.platform.host` | `host` | Refinement of the generic host entity for a physical virtualization platform. A virtualization platform is a bare-metal host server that runs a hypervisor or firmware partitioning technology. The virtualization-specific attributes (system name, firmware version, serial number) extend the generic host description while preserving full compatibility with consumers that understand the base host entity. |
| `refinement.virtualization.vm.host` | `host` | Refinement of the generic host entity for a virtual machine managed by a software hypervisor. A virtualization VM is a software-emulated or paravirtualized guest machine — the distributed equivalent of any cloud compute instance. This refinement ensures that cross-platform consumers that understand the base host entity can navigate VM data using standard host attributes while the VM-specific attributes provide additional context. |


## `refinement.virtualization.partition.host`

Refines upstream entity: `host`

**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)

Refinement of the generic host entity for a firmware-enforced partition. A virtualization partition is a hardware-isolated execution environment — the mainframe equivalent of a virtual machine, but enforced at the firmware level. The partition behaves as an independent host from the perspective of workloads running inside it.

**Type:** `host`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

For Cloud, this must be the instance_id assigned by the cloud provider. For non-containerized systems, this should be the `machine-id`. See the table below for the sources to use to determine the `machine-id` based on operating system. [1] | `fdbf79e8af94cb7f9e8df36789187052` |

**[1] `host.id`:** Collecting `host.id` from non-containerized systems

**Non-privileged Machine ID Lookup**

When collecting `host.id` for non-containerized systems non-privileged lookups
of the machine ID are preferred. SDK detector implementations MUST use the
sources listed below to obtain the machine ID.

| OS | Primary | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux | contents of `/etc/machine-id` | contents of `/var/lib/dbus/machine-id` |
| BSD | contents of `/etc/hostid` | output of `/bin/kenv -q smbios.system.uuid` |
| macOS | `IOPlatformUUID` line from the output of `/usr/sbin/ioreg -rd1 -c "IOPlatformExpertDevice"` | - |
| Windows | `MachineGuid` from registry `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography` | - |

**Privileged Machine ID Lookup**

The `host.id` can be looked up using privileged sources. For example, Linux
systems can use the output of `dmidecode -t system`, `dmidecode -t baseboard`,
`dmidecode -t chassis`, or read the corresponding data from the filesystem
(e.g. `cat /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/product_id`,
`cat /sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/product_uuid`, etc), however, SDK resource
detector implementations MUST not collect `host.id` from privileged sources. If
privileged lookup of `host.id` is required, the value should be injected via the
`OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` environment variable.

**[2] `virtualization.partition.name`:** The partition name as configured in the hypervisor management interface. Not available in the base host entity.

**[3] `host.ip`:** IPv4 Addresses MUST be specified in dotted-quad notation. IPv6 addresses MUST be specified in the [RFC 5952](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5952.html) format.

**[4] `host.mac`:** MAC Addresses MUST be represented in [IEEE RA hexadecimal form](https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/import/documents/tutorials/eui.pdf): as hyphen-separated octets in uppercase hexadecimal form from most to least significant.

**[5] `virtualization.partition.type`:** The workload type or mode of the partition. Not available in the base host entity.

| `scheduling` | Virtual machine has been requested but is waiting for the scheduler to assign it to a host node. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `stopped` | Virtual machine is stopped and not consuming CPU resources. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `succeeded` | Virtual machine completed its workload and terminated cleanly (applicable to batch or ephemeral VMs). | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
